title: SSO/SCIM provisioning + RBAC playbook review with Indigo Therapeutics
summary: Kickoff for SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning and RBAC least-privilege design. Reviewed IdP metadata flow, SCIM attribute mapping, role->group mapping, audit log surface and retention, KMS/encryption options and SOC2 artifacts. Agreed next steps: share SCIM mapping template, SOC2 report, and schedule SAML test in staging next week.
topics: SAML IdP metadata and SP configuration
SCIM provisioning attributes and group sync
RBAC role model and least-privilege boundaries
Audit logs, retention, and export (SIEM integration)
Data residency and private deployment considerations
Pilot/staging test plan and success criteria
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02 16:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood CSM), Dana (Indigo Head of Security), Oliver (Platform), Priya (IT Ops), Marcus (Compliance)

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got about 50 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:08] Dana: Dana here.
[00:10] Oliver: Oliver, platform team.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, IT.
[00:14] Marcus: Marcus, compliance.
[00:16] Aisha: Great. Marco and I are from Redwood — marco will drive the technical parts for SAML and SCIM and i'll cover process and next steps.

[02:02] Marco: OK jumping in, high level — we want to map out two flows: SSO via SAML for user auth and SCIM for provisioning/deprovisioning. We'll also review how groups map to roles in Redwood's RBAC. Any constraints up front?
[02:20] Dana: Our big one is least privilege. We can't have broad admin access. Also we need audit trails that show who triggered provisioning and where tokens are stored, SOC2 evidence, that sort of thing.
[02:36] Aisha: Yup, SOC2 and audit log retention are on the checklist. we maintain an exportable audit log and can forward to your SIEM via syslog or an s3 sink — we'll show examples.

[04:10] Oliver: On the SAML side we're on Okta currently, then we'll have a staging IdP for testing. do you support metadata upload and automatic attribute mapping?
[04:24] Marco: Yes, we accept IdP metadata XML or entityID + SSO URL + certificate. On attributes, we support nameid, email, firstName/lastName, and arbitrary claims for mapping. SCIM is where groups sync happens.
[05:00] Speaker 3: (inaudible) question about group nested groups?
[05:08] Marco: nested groups are tricky — Redwood's SCIM accepts group membership with array of member ids; we don't currently expand nested groups on ingestion, so best practice is to flatten primary groups in IdP or use a SCIM job on Okta to sync flattened groups.

[07:30] Priya: For provisioning we need to ensure deprovisioning is instantaneous when someone leaves. Does SCIM support immediate disable?
[07:45] Marco: SCIM operations include patch/replace and delete. we recommend the user lifecycle hook: when Okta sets active=false we either mark disabled in our system or remove sessions depending on your policy. we can shorten token TTLs for staged users.

[10:12] Marcus: Audit log specifics — we need user change events, provisioning events, role assignment changes, and admin actions. retention required is 7 years for some of our regs — can you hold that?
[10:36] Leah: That's long, most customers choose 1-3 years default. We can provide extended retention as an enterprise add-on and export raw logs to your S3 for long-term archival.
[10:52] Dana: ok export is fine as long as we can attest chain of custody.

[12:00] Aisha: quick note — i'll share our SOC2 Type II report and network diagram after this call, also a redwood secure architecture whitepaper link.
[12:12] Aisha: link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-type2.pdf (placeholder)

[14:05] Oliver: On RBAC modeling — we have dev, svc-ops, infra-admin and compliance-view roles. We want minimal admin users; infra-admin should be tightly controlled. How do you suggest mapping groups to roles?
[14:24] Marco: recommended pattern: 1) Create coarse roles in Redwood (viewer, developer, svc-account, infra-admin). 2) Use SCIM group->role mapping; only map Okta groups that are managed by HR or a small admin team to the infra-admin role. 3) Use just-in-time escalation for temporary admin tasks where possible — we can integrate with an approval workflow via your ticketing tool.

[16:40] Priya: Are there service accounts for CI? how do you handle key rotation?
[16:48] Marco: for CI we recommend service API tokens scoped to minimal actions, stored in your vault. Tokens can be short lived; Redwood supports rotating tokens via our console and programmatic calls. For encryption we support customer-managed keys via KMS (AWS KMS or cloud HSM) and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) patterns.

[18:55] Marcus: Data residency — some of our data must remain in eu-west-1. Does Redwood support region pinning for customer data and logs?
[19:06] Leah: Yes, our private/dedicated offerings allow region pinning; hosted account can be region-restricted on request for enterprise. We also provide an on-prem package but that requires procurement.

[21:30] Dana: On encryption at rest, do you store any plaintext in logs? we need assurance keys are not exfiltrated.
[21:42] Marco: No plaintext storage. Logs are structured and searchable but sensitive fields are redacted by default. We encrypt at rest with AES-256 and keys are protected by KMS; you can choose to manage your KMS keys.

[24:10] Oliver: about SCIM attribute mapping — we'll want to sync title/department and a manager field so we can auto-assign approvers. do you accept custom attributes?
[24:22] Marco: yes, custom attributes are supported. we'll send a SCIM mapping template. For manager relationships SCIM supports 'manager' as a complex attribute but not every IdP populates it consistently — okta does via the manager field if populated in the profile.

[26:45] Aisha: Let's walk through a sample mapping — Marco, can you screen share the mapping doc?
[26:51] Marco: (shares) I'm pulling the template now; list of supported attributes: userName, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type eq "work"].value, active, groups[].display, manager.value

[29:10] (short silence, clicking)
[29:28] Dana: Another ask — SSO session inactivity 30 minutes sounds right for admin sessions. Is session timeout configurable by role?
[29:36] Marco: yes, you can set session TTLs per role and enforce MFA for high-privilege roles. We support MFA via IdP enforced policies and step-up auth for sensitive operations.

[31:00] Priya: On the IdP metadata exchange, what cert algorithms do you accept? RSA-SHA256 ok?
[31:08] Marco: RSA-SHA256 is standard, we also accept ECDSA. If your IdP uses older sha1 we'll flag it as deprecated.

[33:15] Oliver: For the staging test, we want to run a staged rollout: 1) test account provisioning 2) group sync 3) role assignment 4) admin escalation test. timeframe?
[33:28] Aisha: sounds good. we suggest a one-week runway for the staging test. Marco will provide a checklist.

[35:40] Marco: i'll also include a troubleshooting playbook for the common SCIM 409/404 errors and a sample postman collection for SCIM endpoints.

[37:05] Marcus: about compliance evidence — can you provide logs that show role change events with actor and timestamp, in a forensically sound manner?
[37:18] Leah: yes, audit logs include actor, source IP, request id and we can provide a signed export (hashing) for attestation. For long-term retention we recommend S3 export with lifecycle rules.

[40:00] Dana: Any blockers on our side? we need to ensure our Okta admin can create a SCIM connector and we need a service account with minimum permissions to call SCIM.
[40:12] Priya: we'll provision that after the call.

[42:20] Aisha: Quick recap of action items then we'll schedule follow up.
[42:26] Aisha: Next steps — Marco will share SCIM template and SAML metadata steps; Leah will share SOC2 and network diagram; i will send pilot checklist and proposed dates.

[44:00] Oliver: One more — does Redwood support SAML attribute encryption for sensitive attributes?
[44:10] Marco: We support encrypted assertions if your IdP can produce them; it's an enterprise option and we can enable it on your tenant.

[46:30] Dana: Are there any competitor risk notes? we currently evaluate Redwood vs Anthropic-hosted and a managed Sagemaker endpoint.
[46:40] Aisha: noted. we'll highlight our enterprise audit surface and region pinning as differentiators.

[48:05] Priya: For testing, can we get a temporary test tenant and sample keys?
[48:14] Marco: Yes, we'll spin up a staging tenant and provide SP metadata, test credentials and a small test user set.

[50:00] Aisha: ok thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and set the SAML test for next tuesday at 10am PT unless that conflicts.
[50:12] Marcus: That works.
[50:18] Dana: Thanks.
[50:20] Aisha: Thanks all.
[51:00] (meeting ends)
